title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
layout_note: The two approaches are stacked top and bottom in one column-width figure, each named by a large bold title at the right (Fine-tuning on top, Prefix-tuning below), each with the same example token row underneath.
grouping: Per-task copies are grouped by fanning: three offset overlapping cards (one per task, labelled in parentheses) in the top half; in the bottom half a single wide grey card with a small fan of three offset prefix cards overlapping its left end. Colour family: pink/red for what is trained and stored per task, grey for the frozen shared model.
shapes_depth: Flat rectangles with thin dark outlines and no shadows; each model card holds a row of tall empty white slots, one per token position, aligned above the token words below it. Prefix cards are smaller, rounded, pale pink with two tall pink slots inside. The tokens are coloured words, not boxes: input tokens in blue, output tokens in green, with small 'Input (task)' and 'Output (task)' labels under them.
proposed_highlight: The proposed parameters are the only pink in the bottom half: small pink prefix cards beside a large grey pretrained model, against the top half where every full model copy is pink. The bold section titles name the two approaches; no arrows.
lesson: Show per-task storage cost by fanning stacked copies: full model copies fanned in the trainable colour above, versus one grey frozen model with only a small fan of trainable prefix cards beside it, so the size of the fanned thing is the cost.
notes: 'other' element = the fanned, offset card stacks used to show one copy per task. The whole figure is one embedded raster in the PDF (a vector-style diagram exported as an image); kb measure left photo_share null and measured the palette over the whole crop. Venue from Semantic Scholar (ACL); year = venue year 2021, which matches the arXiv preprint year.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: two stacked comparisons with the same token layout: 'Fine-tuning' on top is three overlapping full-size pink Transformer cards (one per task), 'Prefix-tuning' below is one grey pretrained Transformer with three small overlapping pink Prefix cards stacked at its left edge, so whole pink models shrink to small pink prefixes

relations.form: the per-task copies are drawn as offset overlapping cards (Translation, Summarization, Table-to-text) in both halves - full transformers on top, only prefixes below
in the lower half one grey Transformer (Pretrained) card spans the token columns and every task prefix sits in front of its left end
token positions are tall white slots in each card, aligned over a real tokenized example 'name Starbucks type coffee shop [SEP] Starbucks serves coffee' printed beneath each half
the prefix's two pink slots occupy the leftmost token positions of the shared transformer, prepended rather than wired in

channels.colour: pink = task-specific trainable parameters, grey = frozen pretrained parameters (one meaning); in the text example blue = input tokens and green = output tokens
channels.shape: rounded cards = parameter sets (a model or a prefix), tall white slots = token positions
channels.line: no lines or arrows at all
channels.frame: each card frames one parameter set; overlapping stacked cards = one copy per task

quality.strengths: the parameter saving is visible by area and colour alone - three full pink cards versus three small pink prefix cards on one grey card - without reading labels; the same tokenized example under both halves fixes what is held constant; colour has one meaning (trainable vs frozen)
quality.weaknesses: no arrows or layer structure show that the prefix acts on activations at every layer, so the mechanism must be inferred; the prefix cards cover the left end of the transformer, hiding which slots are prefix positions in the shared model; the pink/grey trainable/frozen meaning is not keyed

insights.structure: Two stacked comparisons titled at the top right: 'Fine-tuning' shows three overlapping pink Transformer cards (Translation, Summarization, Table-to-text); 'Prefix-tuning' shows one grey 'Transformer (Pretrained)' with three overlapping small pink Prefix cards stacked at its left edge.
insights.data: Token positions are tall white slots inside each transformer card; the example input and output are a real tokenized sentence below each block, input words in blue and output words in green with '[SEP]' between.
insights.emphasis: Pink = task-specific trainable parameters versus grey = frozen, so the eye sees whole pink models (top) shrink to small pink prefixes (bottom).
insights.flow: Top to bottom comparison; within each block, tokens read left to right with no arrows.
insights.avoid: No arrows show how the prefix interacts with layers (activations at every layer), so the mechanism is inferred only from placement.

arrangement.units: two unframed stacked rows (Fine-tuning, Prefix-tuning) each with fanned overlapping cards for the three tasks
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted tokenized example sentence colored by input/output
arrangement.shared: same example sentence under both rows
